key_insight: A superconducting transmon can be used to deterministically program multipartite entangled states across multiple mechanical phonon modes, not just entangled pairs.
engineering_relevance: This provides a scalable hardware route for multimode quantum memory, simulation, and sensing in compact mechanical resonators.
method: Sequentially apply optimal-control-engineered isometries between a transmon qubit and successive mechanical modes.
Prepare matrix product states of bond dimension two, including W, GHZ, and cluster states.
Use quantum state tomography and correlated-noise sensing to characterize and verify the stored states.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports full tomography and certification of genuine multipartite entanglement among up to four modes, along with quantitative bounds on collective dephasing from sensing measurements.
watch_item: The approach depends on precise optimal control and qubit-mode coherence, which may become harder to maintain as the number of mechanical modes increases.
paper_title: Deterministic and programmable generation of mechanical multipartite entangled states
